Great meeting earlier, Elena — appreciate the clarity on budget and latency needs. Below is a concise cost/TCO-focused recap and three pilot options so your procurement team can pick the right path. I attached a simple spreadsheet with line-item estimates (Redwood_Pilot_Estimate_FinRetail_Q1.xlsx).

Executive summary (quick numbers)
- Observed monthly token volume: 420,000,000 tokens
- Baseline (no optimization) estimate using redwood-medium-1 (hosted): ~ $28,000 / month
- Optimized estimate (batching + prefix caching + KV cache + int8 quantization where acceptable): ~ $9,600 — $12,800 / month
- Dedicated reserved capacity (1x pool sized for peak throughput to meet 99p <250ms): ~ $32,000 / month (SLA + predictable unit economics)

Assumptions and math (high level)
- Average tokens per interaction: 350 tokens (prompt + completion). That implies ~1.2M interactions/month (420M / 350).
- Baseline per-1k-token rate (hosted, mixed prompt/completion) used in model: $0.022 / 1k tokens -> baseline = 420,000k * $0.022 = $9,240 compute-only; additional infrastructure and ephemeral cost, plus safety/observability overheads, drives the working baseline estimate to ~$28k. (Spreadsheet breaks this out.)

Which levers move the needle
- Batching (continuous dynamic batching): reduces per-token compute by increasing GPU utilization; for chat workloads we estimate a ~20-35% reduction in token CPU/GPU usage depending on request concurrency and peak shape. Implication: reduces latency-sensitive cost but must be tuned to avoid increasing p95.
- Prefix / KV caching: for repeated prompts and multi-turn flows KV cache can reduce served tokens by 15-30% on average. This is very effective for templated or FAQ-style dialogs.
- Quantization (INT8/4-bit where appropriate): can reduce model footprint and cost by ~10-20% with some downstream quality testing required.
- Routing to cheaper model variants for lower-risk traffic: offload lower-confidence or bulk operations to smaller models or cached responses to lower unit cost.

Pilot options (pick one)
1) Low-cost pilot (recommended if initial cap = $15k/mo): 2-week technical pilot on hosted Redwood with optimization focus. Scope: 10% of traffic routed to pilot flow; enable batching + prefix caching; run evals to validate quality. Estimated spend: $3k–6k for the 2-week pilot (extrapolated monthly $9–12k if scaled). Success criteria: 25%+ token reduction without measurable quality loss and p95 <300ms on pilot traffic.

2) Proof-of-value pilot (2–4 weeks): larger slice (25% traffic), add quantization experiments and a small dedicated cache. Estimated monthly run-rate if scaled: $10k–14k. Deliverable: performance report, cost delta, recommendation for full rollout.

3) Dedicated reserved pilot and SLA (preferred for strict latency & predictability): 4-week reserved pool sized to meet 99p <250ms. Fixed monthly charge (~$32k) with predictable unit economics and engineering support. Deliverable: SLA-backed pilot and operational runbook.

Procurement & security
- SOC 2 report and standard security package: happy to share immediately (I’ve linked in the Drive folder).
- For PO timing: if you want the low-cost pilot under $15k, we can provision a scoped hosted pilot with a short order form and an exchange of a standard MSA addendum. If you need a PO> $25k and legal review, we’ll involve contracts.

Next steps I propose

- I’ll send a short SOW + order form and the pilot estimate spreadsheet (attached).
- If procurement needs a tighter estimate template, I’ll have Marissa run a final line-item quote you can attach to the PO.
